title: Your Fall Comfort Food Deserves an All-Clad Upgrade
gist: Affiliate-style roundup of All-Clad factory-seconds discounts (29-74% off) ahead of Thanksgiving, with the author's buy-once philosophy. Consumer promo with little market signal.

insights.claim: A full set of All-Clad pots runs about $800, so the author recommends building a collection piece by piece via factory-seconds sales.
insights.speaker: Kat Merck
insights.so_what: Premium cookware demand is supported by discounting of blemished inventory.
insights.locator: All-Clad cookware is a buy-it-for-life staple

insights.claim: The sale offers cookware with packaging damage or minor blemishes at deep discounts, with every piece carrying the regular limited lifetime warranty, but items are limited and all sales are final.
insights.speaker: Kat Merck
insights.so_what: Seconds channel lets premium brand clear inventory without cutting list prices.
insights.quote: huge discounts can be had on cookware that only has packaging damage or a minor blemish

insights.claim: Specific deals include the D3 six-piece set at $400 (29% off), the D3 12-quart stockpot at $180 (57% off) and a 15-inch oval baker at $60 (74% off).
insights.speaker: Kat Merck
insights.so_what: Discount depth varies widely by item, from 29% to 74%.

insights.claim: Wired discloses it may earn compensation from retailers on purchases through its links, so the piece functions as affiliate commerce content.
insights.speaker: Kat Merck
insights.so_what: Affiliate deal content is a revenue line for media outlets.
insights.quote: we may receive compensation from retailers and/or from purchases of products through these links
